headline: Coarse-grained models resolve nucleic acid condensate size, folding, and phase separation
label: Coarse Grained Nucleic Acid Models
summary: Nucleotide-resolved and intermediate-resolution coarse-grained models now address nucleic acid phase separation and folding in heterogeneous systems.
synthesis: The common thread is coarse-grained modeling of nucleic acids, in which reduced representations are used to access condensate and folding behavior relevant to phase separation. Simulations and experiments show hnRNPK and Nucleolin forming distinct condensates, and a nucleotide-resolved RNA model reveals RNA-controlled fusion dynamics that set hnRNPK condensate size. An intermediate-resolution model, iConDNA, captures DNA base stacking and pairing, folds hairpins and duplexes, and qualitatively addresses DNA phase separation. A Martini 3-compatible DNA model, parameterized by Bayesian optimization against all-atom references using a scaled Wasserstein metric, extends this toolkit to heterogeneous molecular systems. What is new is the attention to parameterization and interoperability, namely explicit optimization against atomistic references and compatibility with an established coarse-grained force field.
